newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed with fairly heavy losses as remarks by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing weighed on prices in a previously directionless market.

German and Dutch bond prices closed some 30 basis points lower at the long end after Issing said he saw the German economy remaining strong into 1997 and that there was no reason for further cuts in historically low German interest rates.
"I don't think I would argue with Issing's analysis really, and this probably means we're going to see interest rates creep up as we move into 1997," said one dealer.
But others predicted that bond prices would revisit their January 1996 highs before the year ended.
"We were ripe for a bit of a correction and we might come down another 20 basis points (in prices) but then I think we'll go for the previous highs again," said one.
The same dealer said he was advising clients to stay long for this reason, but added that his advice was going largely unheeded.
